games.title: Chaksakpar (Kite Fighting)
games.description: Bhutanese kite fighting where participants fly kites and attempt to cut opponents' strings using specialized line coated with abrasive mixtures.
howToPlay: Step 1: Players prepare kites and coat strings with abrasive mixture.
Step 2: Kites are launched and maneuvered to gain height advantage.
Step 3: Players cross strings with opponents and cut by sawing motion.
Step 4: The loser's kite floats away, chased by children on ground.
Step 5: Skilled flyers use complex maneuvers to entangle opponents.
Step 6: Multiple kites may compete simultaneously.
Step 7: The last kite flying wins.
Step 8: Kite flying season is eagerly anticipated by children and adults.
Step 9: Different kite designs affect performance.
Step 10: The game builds patience, reflexes, and strategic thinking.

games.title: Chyangma
games.description: A traditional game played in mountain regions using woven bamboo rings. Players throw rings at a target, competing for accuracy.
howToPlay: Step 1: Create rings by weaving bamboo strips into circles.
Step 2: Place a stake or peg in the ground at a distance.
Step 3: Players take turns throwing rings toward the stake.
Step 4: Points awarded for rings that land on or near the stake.
Step 5: Rings that encircle the stake score highest points.
Step 6: Multiple rounds are played with cumulative scoring.
Step 7: Players develop throwing accuracy and touch.
Step 8: The game uses locally available materials.
Step 9: Often played during leisure time in mountain villages.
Step 10: Winners receive recognition within the community.

games.title: Dhyakki (Hopscotch)
games.description: Nepali version of hopscotch, primarily played by girls. Players hop through numbered boxes while kicking a flat stone, testing balance and precision.
equipment: Chalk or stick to draw boxes
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a hopscotch grid with numbered boxes on the ground.
Step 2: Players toss a flat stone into the first box.
Step 3: Hop on one foot through the boxes, avoiding the box with the stone.
Step 4: Kick the stone to the next box while hopping.
Step 5: Continue until reaching the end and turn back.
Step 6: If successful, toss stone to next box and repeat.
Step 7: Player loses turn if stone lands on a line, both feet touch ground, or balance is lost.
Step 8: Player who completes all boxes first wins.
Step 9: Advanced players add complex patterns and faster movements.
Step 10: Singing often accompanies the game.

games.title: Ekka-Dokka
games.description: A traditional hopscotch variant primarily played by girls, using a broken piece of earthen pot (guti). Players hop through numbered boxes while singing a melodious rhyme, kicking the guti through each section.
equipment: Chalk or stick to draw boxes
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a large rectangle divided into six boxes on the ground.
Step 2: Name the boxes: ek-er ghor (first), dui-er ghor (second), etc., with the last called samundra.
Step 3: Players roll their guti into the first box while standing outside.
Step 4: Hop on one foot and kick the guti from box to box in sequence.
Step 5: Continue until reaching the fifth box, then return to start.
Step 6: After completing, roll the guti to the second box and repeat.
Step 7: Players sing the ekka-dokka melody throughout the game.
Step 8: Elimination occurs if guti lands on a line, wrong box, or both feet touch ground.
Step 9: The player who completes all boxes successfully wins.
Step 10: Advanced players add complex patterns and faster movements.

games.title: Feviyya Fathun (Mango Seed Game)
games.description: A children's game using dried mango seeds as playing pieces. Players flick seeds at a target, competing for accuracy and distance.
games.occasion: Mango season, after school, casual play
howToPlay: Step 1: Collect and dry mango seeds after eating the fruit.
Step 2: Mark a throwing line on the ground.
Step 3: Place a target at a predetermined distance.
Step 4: Players take turns flicking or throwing seeds toward the target.
Step 5: Points awarded based on proximity to target.
Step 6: Seeds that hit the target score highest points.
Step 7: Players can knock opponents' seeds away.
Step 8: Multiple rounds are played with cumulative scoring.
Step 9: Seeds are collected and traded among children.
Step 10: Winner receives bragging rights and sometimes opponents' seeds.

games.title: Gutte (Five Stones)
games.description: A traditional game played with five small stones, testing hand-eye coordination and dexterity. Players toss one stone while picking up others from the ground.
howToPlay: Step 1: Scatter five stones on the ground.
Step 2: Toss one stone into the air.
Step 3: While it's airborne, pick up one stone from ground.
Step 4: Catch the falling stone with same hand.
Step 5: Set aside collected stone and repeat until all gathered.
Step 6: Next level requires picking up two stones at once.
Step 7: Higher levels involve picking up three, then four stones.
Step 8: If player drops or fails to catch, turn passes.
Step 9: Player completing all levels wins.
Step 10: Rhymes often accompany gameplay.

games.title: Kancha (Marbles)
games.description: A classic childhood game played with colorful glass marbles, where players use their shooter marble to knock opponents' marbles out of a circle.
howToPlay: Step 1: Draw a circle on flat ground.
Step 2: Each player places several marbles inside the circle.
Step 3: Players take turns shooting their shooter marble from outside the circle.
Step 4: Flick the shooter with thumb to knock marbles out.
Step 5: Keep any marbles knocked out of the circle.
Step 6: If shooter stays inside, player continues; if not, turn passes.
Step 7: Game continues until all marbles are cleared.
Step 8: Player with most marbles collected wins.
Step 9: Special marbles are prized and traded.
Step 10: Advanced techniques include backspin and curve shots.

games.title: Khuru (Dart Game)
games.description: A traditional Bhutanese dart game played outdoors with heavy wooden darts and a small softwood target. Players throw darts underhand at a target about 20 meters away, often accompanied by friendly wagers.
games.occasion: Festivals, gatherings, archery matches, leisure time
howToPlay: Step 1: A small cylindrical target made of softwood is placed about 20 meters away.
Step 2: Teams or individuals gather, often with traditional drinks and snacks.
Step 3: Players take turns throwing heavy wooden darts underhand toward the target.
Step 4: The dart must stick into the target to score points.
Step 5: Points are awarded based on where the dart lands on the target.
Step 6: Teammates cheer and tease opponents in good-natured banter.
Step 7: Matches often involve small bets or prizes.
Step 8: The game requires precision and consistent throwing technique.
Step 9: Skilled players are respected in their communities.
Step 10: Khuru is often played alongside traditional archery matches.

games.title: Kula Gaddu (Tops Game)
games.description: A traditional spinning top game where children carve wooden tops and compete in spinning duration and battling other tops.
howToPlay: Step 1: Children carve wooden tops from local wood or purchase them.
Step 2: Wind string around the top from bottom to top.
Step 3: Throw the top while pulling the string to make it spin.
Step 4: Compete to see whose top spins the longest.
Step 5: In battle mode, players try to knock opponents' tops out of a ring.
Step 6: Tops can be decorated with colors and patterns.
Step 7: Skilled players develop techniques for powerful spins.
Step 8: Tops that spin longest or knock out others win.
Step 9: Game develops hand-eye coordination and technique.
Step 10: Winners collect opponents' tops as prizes.

games.title: Pancha Demeema
games.description: A traditional game played with five small seashells, a coconut shell, and a pancha chart. Tests hand-eye coordination and counting skills.
howToPlay: Step 1: Players sit around a flat surface with the equipment.
Step 2: Seashells are tossed and patterns are observed.
Step 3: Points are awarded based on how shells land.
Step 4: The coconut shell is used as a target or container.
Step 5: Players take turns tossing and collecting.
Step 6: The pancha chart guides scoring.
Step 7: Requires concentration and precise tossing.
Step 8: Often played during Avurudu celebrations.
Step 9: Passed down through generations.
Step 10: Combines chance with skill.

games.title: Phobjur
games.description: A traditional archery variation where competitors shoot at small wooden targets from great distances, incorporating elaborate celebrations and team camaraderie.
howToPlay: Step 1: Teams assemble with traditional bamboo bows and arrows.
Step 2: Small wooden targets are placed at distances up to 140 meters.
Step 3: Teams take turns shooting at the targets.
Step 4: Hits are celebrated with group dances and songs.
Step 5: Women often perform mocking dances to distract opponents.
Step 6: Points are awarded for hitting the target.
Step 7: The game continues until a team reaches a winning score.
Step 8: Elaborate celebrations follow each hit.
Step 9: Traditional food and drinks accompany matches.
Step 10: Archery is considered Bhutan's national sport.

games.title: Pundo
games.description: A traditional game similar to bowling, played with flat stones. Players slide stones along the ground toward a target stone, competing for accuracy.
howToPlay: Step 1: A target stone is placed at one end of a smooth playing area.
Step 2: Players stand at a marked throwing line.
Step 3: Each player slides their flat stone along the ground toward the target.
Step 4: Points are awarded based on how close the stone lands to the target.
Step 5: Players can knock opponents' stones away from the target.
Step 6: The player whose stone is closest after all throws scores.
Step 7: Multiple rounds are played with cumulative scoring.
Step 8: Players develop touch and control for precise sliding.
Step 9: The game requires minimal equipment and space.
Step 10: Friendly competition and socializing accompany the game.

games.title: Ran Maa (Gold Leaf Game)
games.description: A traditional game using woven palm leaves, where players create intricate patterns and compete in design complexity and speed of weaving.
howToPlay: Step 1: Collect and prepare dried palm leaves.
Step 2: Cut leaves into uniform strips.
Step 3: Players weave strips into predetermined patterns.
Step 4: Competition based on speed of weaving.
Step 5: Alternatively, judges evaluate design complexity and beauty.
Step 6: Traditional patterns are taught by elders to youth.
Step 7: Completed weavings can be used as decorations.
Step 8: Game preserves traditional craft skills.
Step 9: Winners recognized for their craftsmanship.
Step 10: Often played during cultural festivals.

games.title: Soksum
games.description: A traditional game involving throwing a wooden stick through a moving wheel, testing timing and accuracy. Often played during festivals and celebrations.
howToPlay: Step 1: A large wooden wheel is rolled along the ground by one player.
Step 2: Other players stand at a distance with small sticks or spears.
Step 3: As the wheel passes, players attempt to throw their sticks through the moving wheel's spokes.
Step 4: Successful throws that pass through score points.
Step 5: Players take turns rolling the wheel and throwing.
Step 6: The game requires precise timing and aim.
Step 7: Multiple rounds are played with cumulative scoring.
Step 8: Skilled players can hit the wheel consistently.
Step 9: The game tests hand-eye coordination under dynamic conditions.
Step 10: Winners receive recognition and sometimes small prizes.
